opening_message:
Ticket 1: Nathaniel Young (employee ID E031) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E031.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Nathaniel Young (E031) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. As a full-time employee he is eligible for write (up to write; admin only if role owns the system, which applies here but write was requested). Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security record for E031 (Nathaniel Young) shows contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training; never admin. Requested write > max, so recommend read. (Note: this conflicts with the earlier note listing full-time.)
reason: Nathaniel Young (E031) requests write access to Payroll. The HR note identifies him as a full-time employee and Payroll Specialist (checked in HR's database). Full-time employees may have up to write, and admin only if their role owns the system; his role (Payroll Specialist) owns Payroll, so write is within policy. Although the Security note lists him as a contractor with basic training (which would cap at read), the two notes conflict on employment type. HR is the authoritative source for employment status, and the HR database confirms full-time employment. Since write was requested and is at or below the maximum for a full-time Payroll Specialist, grant write.
